newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel sees breakeven in 1996, good profit by '98.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees breakeven in 1996, good profit by '98.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom said it aims to break even for the full year 1996 and expects a return to good profitability by 1998.
Chairman Serge Tchuruk told reporters that, after the sale of Alcatel's 25 percent stake in Cofira, its 1996 profit including capital gains would be "several billion francs".

Alcatel reported a net loss of 0.4 billion francs for the first half of 1996, compared with a loss of 1.2 billion francs last year. It said the narrowing of the half-year loss was in line with its action plan but noted the effects of a recovery plan introduced last year were still limited.

"The board also noticed that the effects of the plan, already more noticeable for the second half, enabled the group to aim at a return to break-even for the whole year and to foresee a significant reduction in debt, taking into account the divestments already completed as of today," the company said in its first-half earnings statement.
It said the group maintained its objective to achieve savings of seven billion francs per year by 1998.
Tchuruk told a news conference, "We maintain our objective for re-establishing Alcatel's profitability at a good level."
